findings.title: Inbound mail HTML reaches the forward/reply editor initial content without the sanitizer every sibling render sink applies
findings.proofLevel: RUNTIME_VERIFIED (filter survivor set + authenticated-page DOM delivery; editor-iframe execution not demonstrated)
findings.preconditions: Inbound mail with attacker-chosen HTML body (any deployment with mail ingestion configured); an agent opens the forward/reply editor for that mail.
findings.positiveControl: Sibling automatic sinks on the same data are guarded: v-safe-html at view.blade.php:246, strip_tags at DataGrid.php:472; the filter's controls behave (on* stripped, script/iframe removed, javascript: URIs rewritten).
findings.negativeControl: The sole filter (HtmlFilter::process, the same call ingestion makes) was probed with 9 payload classes on the deployed runtime; the survivor set was measured precisely (SMIL animate/set, data:text/html URIs pass; style emptied).
findings.observedImpact: External mail sender's script-class markup reaches the authenticated agent session's editor surface (stored reply captured verbatim in the live page DOM as the editor data source).
findings.notDemonstrated: End-to-end click execution inside the TinyMCE 6.6.2 editor iframe (composer did not mount for the hand-crafted row in the lab).

findings.title: acl.php leaves destructive attribute routes unmapped and the Bouncer dotted-prefix ancestor fallback authorizes them, while exact-mapped sibling deletes stay permission-gated
findings.proofLevel: RUNTIME_VERIFIED (end-to-end HTTP for attribute mass-destroy; reflection-level for the additional cross-domain grants)
findings.preconditions: Role granting only a view/ancestor ACL key such as settings.automation.attributes (supported configuration, no write keys); acl.php has no mapping for the write route (shipped default).
findings.positiveControl: Exact-mapped DELETE /admin/settings/attributes/<id> returns 401 for the same session; exact view key returns 200.
findings.negativeControl: leads.view holder DENIED admin.leads.quotes.delete — the walk stops at the mapped admin.leads.quotes. prefix, showing the walk is bounded by existing mappings, which is exactly why unmapped routes fall through.
findings.observedImpact: View-only role hard-deleted 2 of 3 admin-created attribute definitions via POST mass-destroy (HTTP 200) with FK-CASCADE destruction of all stored attribute_values; reflection confirms leads.view -> admin.leads.attributes.update/emails.store and products.view -> admin.products.inventories.store/admin.products.search.
findings.notDemonstrated: HTTP-level execution of the reflection-confirmed additional grants; introducing commit not traced.

findings.title: The data-transfer import delete path resolves row targets without the authorized-user scope the interactive delete route enforces
findings.preconditions: Initiator holds the two import ACL keys with limited view_permission (individual, authorized ids = self); rows target records outside the initiator's authorized ids (ids enumerable).
findings.positiveControl: Same user's interactive GET edit/{admin-owned id} returns 401 (preventUnauthorizedAccess); the admin-owned person does not appear in the user's datagrid.
findings.negativeControl: First reproduction attempt with a wrong column set failed closed (wrong_columns_number, 0 rows processed) — the pipeline's own validation behaves; the corrected CSV then deletes cross-scope.
findings.observedImpact: Restricted user U2 started a persons action=delete import: summary deleted=2, admin-owned person id 62 hard-deleted (4 attribute_values rows orphaned), entirely bypassing the scope the UI enforces.
findings.notDemonstrated: Only the persons importer driven end-to-end; leads/products/quotes importers share the unscoped pattern but were not executed.

findings.title: The lead person-attach path persists person ids without re-asserting the actor's authorized-user scope, while the direct person read path enforces it
findings.preconditions: Actor holds lead-edit rights under individual/group view_permission; a person outside the actor's authorized-user-ids exists (ids enumerable).
findings.positiveControl: Direct GET /admin/contacts/persons/view/<victim id> returns 401 for the same user; the same person[id] payload at another user's lead returns 401.
findings.negativeControl: The lead update path itself is scope-gated for the lead id (cross-user lead target rejected) — only the person id inside the payload goes unchecked.
findings.observedImpact: PUT attributes/edit/<own lead> with person[id]=<victim id> persisted (HTTP 200); the lead view HTML and kanban JSON render the victim person's email and contact number verbatim.
findings.notDemonstrated: Write access to the victim lead; victim attribute-file contents not accessed.

findings.title: The export writer returns stored cell values verbatim while the JSON datagrid path strips them (CSV/XLSX formula injection)
findings.proofLevel: RUNTIME_VERIFIED (CSV raw bytes + XLSX formula element + server-side evaluation attempt)
findings.preconditions: Any record-creating actor (incl. anonymous public web-form submission) seeds a field value with a leading =/+/-/@; a staff member exports and opens the file in spreadsheet software.
findings.positiveControl: The JSON datagrid path for the same rows applies strip_tags (sanitizeRow) — the export branch is the bypass.
findings.negativeControl: Non-formula-leading seeded values export unchanged and inert; only =/+/-/@ leading values carry the injection class.
findings.observedImpact: CSV bytes carry "=VERIFY(1)+1 <tag>" raw with no quote-prefix; XLSX sheet1.xml contains <c r="B3" t="str"><f>VERIFY(1)+1 …</f><v>0</v></c> and the writer attempts server-side evaluation during calculateColumnWidths (dummy formula can crash the export with TypeError 500).
findings.notDemonstrated: Client-side formula evaluation on the analyst's machine (spreadsheet application settings are a client fact outside this repository).

findings.title: The activity file upload path stores payloads of any type and size on the public disk, while mail attachments land on a private disk behind an authenticated download route
findings.preconditions: Any authenticated staff user who can create activities; default public filesystem disk with /storage/* served unauthenticated (shipped defaults).
findings.positiveControl: Mail attachments land on a private disk behind an authenticated download route — the guarded sibling pattern exists in the same product.
findings.negativeControl: PHP execution NOT achievable: content-sniffing hashName() stores PHP-ish content without a .php extension (the polyglot/.php-persistence hypothesis was runtime-refuted during adjudication).
findings.observedImpact: Authenticated uploads of (a) .php-named PHP-ish dummy, (b) .php-named plain text, (c) 2 MB dummy all returned HTTP 200 with zero validation; payloads physically landed under storage/app/public/activities/<id>/; unauthenticated GETs of the /storage/... URLs returned 200 echoing the bytes with content types following the stored names (text/plain, text/html, image/svg+xml).
findings.notDemonstrated: Server-side code execution; demonstrated result is world-readable hosting of attacker-chosen content (stored-XSS/defacement delivery from the origin).

findings.title: The layout renders the stored custom_scripts value outside the escaping every neighbouring template value goes through
findings.proofLevel: RUNTIME_VERIFIED (browser execution confirmed in real Chromium)
findings.preconditions: Actor holding settings/configuration write rights saves the configuration key once (admin-originated value; the boundary crossed is admin -> every subsequent unauthenticated visitor).
findings.positiveControl: Neighbouring template values in the same layouts go through Blade escaping; registered configuration keys pass sanitizeConfigValue's HTMLPurifier.
findings.negativeControl: Undefined keys persist only when getConfigField() returns null (no validation rule rejects them) — the guard exists for known keys, which is exactly why undefined keys fall through raw.
findings.observedImpact: POST configuration store persisted three undefined keys verbatim into core_config; the unauthenticated login page echoed custom_javascript raw inside <script> and custom_css raw inside <style>; real Chromium executed the benign payload document.title='VF3EXECUTED' on /login (tab title changed from 'Sign In'; alert()-variant fired interactively on an earlier load); admin dashboard and public web-form layouts echo the same values raw.
findings.notDemonstrated: Session theft or a malicious payload (only the benign executing-class marker was run).
